_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every number the site claims about itself.
Phase 2.3. Before this existed, the site claimed anywhere from 100 to 22,000 students
across 82 pages, a 44x spread, plus four founding years. Cross-page consistency is a
named trust signal for AI engines: when a site cannot agree with itself, every number on
it gets discounted, including the true ones.
1. Any new page pulls its numbers from here. Never hand-type a stat into a page.
2. Only put a number here you could defend to a journalist or a regulator.
3. A sub-group can never exceed the whole. No single country, age or course may claim
more students than 'students'. (2,400+ German and 3,100+ 8-year-olds are fine
against 10,000+; they were impossible against the 500+ that was briefly considered.)
4. 'rating' comes from Google Business Profile REVIEWS. It is NOT 'rated by N students'.
Say 'rated 4.9 across 547 Google reviews'. That is the claim you can evidence.

_owner_decisions.batchSizes.group: Owner set 5-10 on 2026-09-03, resolving a three-way contradiction: this file said 5-8, 103 course FAQ answers said 'capped at 10', and the board-prep series said 'group 10 to 15' (commit 77f3bf39). The course FAQs were right. Board-prep is NOT covered by this ruling: it is a different product whose 10-15 was set deliberately nine days earlier, and it stays until the owner says otherwise. RECONCILIATION IS OUTSTANDING: 831 files carry 3,367 instances of the old 5-8 claim, in numeric ('5-8 students', '5–8 learners per batch') and written-out ('a batch of five to eight students') forms. It was NOT swept automatically because that is the site's core value proposition, not a label, and some instances are arguments rather than statements ('as long as the batch is genuinely small, five to eight children with a real mentor'). Changing 5-8 to 5-10 makes the batch sound larger, so the copy needs a human pass, not a regex. Guarded script and inventory in seo/superseo-2026-09/. Note 'Grades 5-8' and 'Class 5-8' also appear and must never be caught by such a sweep.
_owner_decisions.students: Owner set 10,000+ on 2026-07-15. Cross-checks: 547 Google reviews against 10,000+ students is a ~5.5% review rate, which is normal; 500+ would imply a >100% review rate. It also matches /about, seo-config.js and the 65 existing on-page claims.
_owner_decisions.founded: 2020, matches schema.org foundingDate and /about. Pages saying 2019/2021/2022 were drift.
_owner_decisions.reviews: 547 real Google reviews. Do not round, do not inflate, and never restate as a student count.
_owner_decisions.countries: Owner set 25+ on 2026-07-15. The site had been saying 15+ (68 uses), 30+ (7), 11/eleven (5) and 25+ (3) at once. The 11 was stale, its enumerated list predates the Gulf cluster and was missing exactly Qatar and Saudi Arabia. NOTE: only 14 country LANDING PAGES exist, which is a page-coverage gap, not a contradiction, students come from more countries than we have pages for. That gap is a content opportunity, not a correction.
_owner_decisions.ages: Owner set 6 to 67 on 2026-07-18: coding AND maths to all ages, 6 to 67; kids category starts at 6. Retired '6-65' and the contradictory homepage/pricing/about/contact ranges (6-18,8-18,6-21,8 to 21+). Kids enrollment floor moved 8->6 (aged 8-12 -> aged 6-12). Pedagogical 'age 8 is ideal to begin block coding' copy left as-is on purpose (opinion, not an enrollment floor) - owner to review separately.

_needs_owner_confirmation.dps_families: 14 DPS pages clone 'Join 500+ families from Delhi's top schools'. Left alone: 500 < 10,000 so it breaks no rule here, but it is an unevidenced subset claim worth confirming.
